messages:
alex.s (sales): Hey team — large fintech prospect asking for a pricing structure: reserved capacity + burst overage protection + some committed credits. Need product input on feasible packaging and a quote by EOW (Fri). They want to avoid unexpected bills.

maria.p (pm): Thanks. Quick clarifying q's: expected QPS or tokens/day? region? compliance needs (SOC2/HIPAA)? are they asking for Dedicated or Private?

sam.k (support): Customer context: onboarding next quarter, regulated data but no full on-prem requirement yet. Pilot will be ~10M tokens/day, spiky during business hours (x3 baseline). Primary ask is a hard overage cap and predictable monthly spend for forecasts.

maria.p (pm): OK useful. Two product-viable patterns we can offer: 1) Reserved pool (committed throughput) + burst buffer billed at a higher per-token rate but with a monthly cap; 2) Committed credits pre-bought + overage charged only if credits exhausted, with auto-fallback to a cheaper serverless model when breach. Pros/cons to weigh.

jenna.t (product-ops): We need launch criteria: SLAs (latency/availability), billing transparency (per-token breakdown), audit logs + KMS for keys. Also legal needs T&Cs for overage forgiveness mechanics. Suggest a checklist before we hand to sales.

alex.s (sales): They specifically asked: can we do a hard $ cap on overages (e.g., stop accepting requests after $X), or at least notify + throttle? They prefer hard cap.

maria.p (pm): Hard cap is operationally tricky for hosted customers but doable for Dedicated with circuit-breaker routing. For hosted, we can implement auto-throttle + notification; stopping requests requires a strict account-level block flow and SLA implications. Which do they prefer?

sam.k (support): Customer prefers hard cap to avoid surprise spend. Willing to accept limited degradation (queueing/throttling) after cap, not full outage.

devon.f (finops): Needcto run numbers. Rough sketch: assume committed 10M tokens @ $0.003/token = $30k/month. Burst tokens billed at $0.005/token with cap at $10k. Effective blended rate depends on burst utilization. Example calc below.

```
Committed_cost = committed_tokens * base_rate
Burst_cost = min(burst_tokens * burst_rate, burst_cap)
Total = Committed_cost + Burst_cost
Effective_rate = Total / (committed_tokens + actual_burst)
```

devon.f (finops): If actual_burst = 2M, then Committed_cost=10M*0.003=$30k, Burst_cost=2M*0.005=$10k (hits cap) => Total=$40k => effective ~ $0.004/token. Margin modeling needs to assume worst-case burst to size infra.

maria.p (pm): Good. From product requirements: we need: billing UI for cap setting, notification hooks (webhook + email), throttle policy (queue length, reject vs delay), and docs on behavior. Put a simple default policy in the pilot, allow customizations post-contract.

infra-bot: Included docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/billing/caps and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/overage-throttle (access: product + eng).

jenna.t (product-ops): I'll draft a one-pager (requirements + acceptance criteria) and a short rollout plan for pilot. Needs eng scope for: billing enforcement, telemetry, and an admin toggle. Dev can we estimate effort? @maria.p assigning eng triage after we confirm pilot scope.

maria.p (pm): Priority guidance: if legal signs off on hard cap with throttle semantics, mark this P1 for pilot. Otherwise P2 with auto-throttle only. Acceptance criteria for P1 pilot: 1) billing cap UI + enforced cap, 2) webhook notification + in-console alerts, 3) transparent post-hoc invoice export, 4) latency SLO maintained for reserved traffic under normal load.

alex.s (sales): Customer wants the quote by Friday. Can we give two options (P1 and P2) with estimated pricing bands?

devon.f (finops): I'll produce quick banded quote: Option A (Reserved + Hard-caped burst) — committed 10M @ $0.0028/token + burst billable to $10k cap @ $0.0048/token => estimate $38k/mo worst case. Option B (Committed credits + fallback) — credits 10M @ $0.003/token + fallback serverless at $0.006/token => estimate $42k/mo worst case but cheaper baseline. Numbers rough, need exact infra cost calc.

maria.p (pm): Sounds fine as an initial estimate. Alex, I recommend offering Option A for pilot (closer to their ask) and be explicit about throttle behavior. Jenna will own the PRD + acceptance checklist; Devon will own the financial calc; Sam will own customer comms. I'll open a product intake item and tag eng for scoping.

jenna.t (product-ops): I'll add the intake item now and link it here. https://redwood.internal/roadmap/requests/INT-4931 : short summary + attachments.

maria.p (pm): Great. @devon.f can you drop final numbers by Thu EOD? @jenna.t will attach acceptance criteria. Alex please confirm customer is OK with throttle-vs-stop semantic.

alex.s (sales): Confirmed — they'll accept throttling with clear notification and a configurable cap. I'll update contract notes. :thumbsup:

maria.p (pm): Thanks everyone — moving to backlog and tagging for kickoff.

sam.k (support): Noted, I'll sync with customer and send them the pilot behavior doc once ready.

alex.s (sales): Appreciated — will ping legal for the clause wording.

jenna.t (product-ops): Looping in eng after intake triage. Closing thread for now. :wave:
